title: Notes on the ideal arithmetic correlations of $N$-ary sequences
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the nonexistence of $N$-ary sequences with ideal arithmetic correlation. We prove that there exist no ternary, quaternary, or $6$-ary sequences with ideal arithmetic autocorrelation when the connection integer is an odd prime power $p^{t}$ and $\textup{ord}_{p^{t}}(N)=\phi(p^{t})/4$, where $\phi$ denotes Euler's totient function. Furthermore, when the connection integer is an odd prime $p$ and  $\textup{ord}_{p}(N)=\phi(p)/6$, no such ternary, quaternary, or $6$-ary sequences exist for ideal arithmetic correlation. This includes in particular the case $p\equiv7(\textup{mod}12)$, for which $\textup{ord}_{p}(N)=\phi(p)/6$ and we further show that no $N$-ary sequence with ideal arithmetic correlation exists for any prime $N>2$. These results provide further evidence that ideal arithmetic correlation is highly restrictive in the $N$-ary setting.

                                        Abstract
     In this paper, we investigate the nonexistence of N -ary sequences with ideal
     arithmetic correlation. We prove that there exist no ternary, quaternary, or 6-ary
     sequences with ideal arithmetic autocorrelation when the connection integer is an
     odd prime power pt and ordpt (N ) = ϕ(pt )/4, where ϕ denotes Euler’s totient
     function. Furthermore, if ordpt (N ) = ϕ(pt )/6 or ϕ(pt )/8, then no such ternary,
     quaternary, or 6-ary sequence families with connection integer pt exist. This
     includes in particular the case p ≡ 7(mod12), for which ordpt (N ) = ϕ(pt )/6;
     we further show that no N -ary sequence families with ideal arithmetic autocor-
     relation exist for any prime N > 2. These results provide further evidence that
     ideal arithmetic correlation is highly restrictive in the N -ary setting. We also
     establish an upper bound on the arithmetic correlation of N -ary sequences.

     Keywords: FCSR sequences, Arithmetic correlation, Nonbinary sequence, Connection
     integer




1 Introduction
Pseudorandom sequences produced by feedback shift registers (FSR) are widely used
in communication systems and stream ciphers [1–3]. Among the various shift-register
models, the feedback with carry shift register (FCSR), introduced by Goresky, Klap-
per, and Xu in the 1990s, has received considerable attention [3–5]. The FCSR can be


                                             1
viewed as an analogue of the linear feedback shift register (LFSR) with an additional
carry mechanism. Among the parameters used to evaluate FCSR sequences, the N -adic
complexity and the arithmetic correlation are of particular importance. The concept
of arithmetic autocorrelation was originally proposed by Mandelbaum in connection
with arithmetic codes [6]. Subsequently, Goresky and Klapper extended this concept
to FCSR sequences and established its relevance in their analysis [3, 7]. These quanti-
ties provide useful criteria for assessing the randomness and cryptographic suitability
of such sequences.

    Recently, the arithmetic correlation of FCSR sequences has received renewed atten-
tion. Studies have addressed the arithmetic correlation of m-sequences [8–11] and
half-ℓ-sequences [12–14], as well as the concept of ideal arithmetic correlation [14–16].
    The main purpose of this paper is to study the nonexistence of N -ary sequences
with ideal arithmetic correlation, that is, sequences whose arithmetic correlation are
equal to zero at every nontrivial shift. Motivated by Edemskiy’s results on the imbal-
ance and ideal arithmetic autocorrelation of N -ary half-ℓ-sequences [14], we establish
several nonexistence results. Our approach is based on the partial sums of Legendre
symbols and the imbalance property of the sequences. More precisely, we rule out the
existence of 3-ary, 4-ary, and 6-ary sequences with ideal arithmetic autocorrelation in
the cases of odd prime-power connection integers pt with ordpt (N ) = ϕ(pt )/4 for sin-
gle sequence, and odd prime-power connection integers pt with ordpt (N ) = ϕ(pt )/6
or ordpt (N ) = ϕ(pt )/8 for sequence families; moreover, if p ≡ 7 (mod 12), no such
sequence exists for any prime N > 2 and ordpt (N ) = ϕ(pt )/6 for sequence families.
We further derive an upper bound for the arithmetic correlation of N -ary sequences,
generalizing the existing binary case.
    The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. In Section 2, we recall
the necessary preliminaries on arithmetic correlation. Section 3 considers the case
ordpt (N ) = ϕ(pt )/4 and proves the nonexistence of 3-ary, 4-ary, and 6-ary sequences
with ideal arithmetic autocorrelation. Section 4 treats the cases ordpt (N ) = ϕ(pt )/6
and ordpt (N ) = ϕ(pt )/8 for sequence families. Section 5 is devoted to deriving an
upper bound on the arithmetic correlation of N -ary sequences. Section 6 concludes
the paper.

6 Conclusion
In this paper, we studied the nonexistence of N -ary sequences with ideal arithmetic
correlations. We obtained several nonexistence results in the cases ordpt (N ) = ϕ(pt )/4,
ordpt (N ) = ϕ(pt )/6 and ordpt (N ) = ϕ(pt )/8, excluding in particular the 3-ary, 4-
ary, and 6-ary cases, and we also proved a nonexistence result for prime N > 2
when p ≡ 7 (mod 12) and ordpt (N ) = ϕ(pt )/6. These results highlight the strong
constraints imposed by ideal arithmetic correlation in the N -ary setting. We have
also established a non-trivial upper bound on the arithmetic correlation of N -ary
sequences, generalizing the result for binary sequences and showing that it applies
when the smallest prime factor pq of q is sufficiently large. It would be of interest to
investigate whether similar nonexistence phenomena hold under other order conditions
or for more general classes of connection integers.
